_comment: The canonical /command grammar, as cases rather than as a regex.
The @mention grammar already exists three times - Node's transformers.js,
Django's comment_mentions.py and Go's mentions_parse.go - held together by
a drift test that reads the others off disk. Commands will duplicate the
same way the moment bots need to type them, since that send path is Go.
A drifted mention notifies the wrong person. A drifted command runs, or
fails to run, something with an effect. So the agreement is pinned here as
INPUTS AND EXPECTED OUTPUTS, which every implementation can execute, rather
than as a pattern every implementation has to translate correctly.
Any new implementation should read this file and run every case. Skip the
suite if the file is absent, the way the Go drift test skips when the
platform sources are not on disk - a missing corpus is a checkout problem,

matches.why: everything after the name is arguments, untouched but trimmed
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: a target narrows fan-out to one bot
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: mobile keyboards capitalise the first letter, so case cannot matter
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: the target is a handle, and handles resolve case-insensitively
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: leading whitespace is a paste artefact, not a decision
matches.name: stop

matches.why: hyphens are in the name charset, matching the model validator
matches.name: my-command

matches.why: internal spacing in arguments is the sender's, not ours to collapse
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: a newline separates the name from its arguments like any space
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: handles may contain dots, underscores and hyphens
matches.name: wake

matches.why: trailing whitespace is trimmed from arguments
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: a name at the maximum length still parses
matches.name: abcdefghijabcdefghijabcdefghijab

matches.why: a command after a mention - the case people actually type, and the reason this is no longer anchored to the start
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: anywhere a word starts, exactly like a mention
matches.name: summarize

matches.why: the FIRST command wins, so there is still one per message
matches.name: stop

matches.why: a target still narrows fan-out when the command follows text
matches.name: summarize

nonMatches.why: a doubled slash is the escape hatch for writing a command name without running it
a slash and a space name nothing
the name must end at whitespace, a target, or the message - so trailing punctuation does not silently become part of it
a colon with no target is a typo, not a command with an empty target
underscores are not in the NAME charset, though they are allowed in a target handle
33 characters - one past the model's limit, so a name that could never exist does not parse
a path, not a command - the second slash is not in the name charset
a date, for the same reason
a slash inside a word is not a command - there is no whitespace before it
the doubled-slash escape hatch still holds mid-sentence
a bare slash after text names nothing
